sections.h1Accent: Zapier and Make.com Workflows Built Right

body.text: Teknoppy provides Zapier automation services and Make.com automation for businesses that want their apps to work together without manual copying, exporting or chasing. We plan, build, fix and maintain Zaps and Make scenarios that connect your website, CRM, email, spreadsheets, payments and messaging tools.
Our in-house team works from Thykoodam, Kochi, for clients in Kerala, across India and overseas.

sections.trustline: Reviewed by Sanal Edison, Founder, Teknoppy. Last updated: 17 November 2026.

paragraphs.text: Zapier and Make.com are no-code platforms that connect thousands of apps. When something happens in one app, such as a new form entry, payment or email, they automatically carry out actions in others. Small teams can automate useful tasks without hiring developers, and larger teams can connect departments quickly.
The challenge is building workflows that stay reliable as volumes grow and apps change. That is where our Zapier automation services help.

What is Make.com? Formerly called Integromat, Make is a visual automation platform where workflows, called scenarios, are drawn as connected modules. It handles complex branching, loops, data transformation and error routes well, often at a lower cost per operation than Zapier for heavier workflows.

Zapier vs Make comes down to simplicity versus flexibility. Zapier is quicker to learn, has the largest app library and suits straightforward workflows. Make offers more visual control, advanced data handling and better value for complex, high-volume scenarios. Many businesses use one or the other; some use both for different jobs.

sections.h2: Zapier or Make for Small Business?

paragraphs.text: Zapier or Make for small business? If you want a few simple automations your team can manage, Zapier is usually the easier choice. If your workflows involve many steps, conditions or large data volumes, Make often costs less and handles the logic better. We recommend a platform after looking at your actual tasks.

items.title: Zapier Workflow Setup
items.html: Zapier workflow setup covers planning, building, testing and documenting Zaps for tasks such as sending website leads to your CRM, adding new customers to email lists, creating invoices from payments and posting alerts to your team.

items.title: Zapier Integrations
items.text: Zapier integrations connect popular tools such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, HubSpot, Zoho, Shopify, WooCommerce, Razorpay, Stripe, Slack, Mailchimp and Calendly. Where an app lacks a built-in integration, we use webhooks or APIs.

items.title: Zapier Webhooks
items.text: Zapier webhooks receive data from systems that are not in Zapier's library, such as custom websites or industry software, and send data to them. We validate incoming data, so bad or incomplete entries do not cause errors downstream.

items.title: Zapier AI Automation
items.text: Zapier AI automation adds AI steps to workflows, for example summarising enquiries, extracting details from emails, classifying support requests or drafting replies for review. We use built-in AI features or connect AI models directly, depending on accuracy and cost needs.

items.title: Fix Broken Zaps
items.text: Many clients contact us to fix broken Zaps. Common causes include expired app connections, changed form fields, filters that no longer match and task limits. We diagnose the cause, repair the workflow and add alerts so future failures are caught early.

items.title: Zapier Cost Optimization
items.text: Zapier cost optimization reviews your account for wasted tasks, such as Zaps that run when nothing needs to happen, duplicated workflows and steps that could be combined. Small changes often reduce monthly task use noticeably.

items.title: Make.com Scenarios
items.text: Our Make.com automation work includes building Make.com scenarios for multi-step processes, such as order processing, inventory updates, lead routing and report generation, with error handlers so problems are caught and retried.

items.title: Make.com Google Sheets Automation
items.text: Make.com Google Sheets automation suits teams that run key processes in spreadsheets. Scenarios can import data, clean it, update rows, trigger alerts and push updates back to other tools on a schedule.

paragraphs.text: As a Make.com automation agency, we also review and improve existing scenarios built by your team or previous providers.

How much does Zapier cost? Zapier has a free plan for basic two-step Zaps and paid plans priced by the number of tasks used each month, with higher tiers adding multi-step Zaps, premium apps and team features. Make prices by operations, which can work out cheaper for complex workflows. Your cost depends on how many tasks or operations your workflows use, so we estimate usage before building.

sections.intro: Some common Zapier automation examples we build:

items.text: Website form submissions added to the CRM, with an instant email and WhatsApp alert to sales
New online orders creating invoices in accounting software
Calendar bookings triggering reminders and adding attendees to a list
Support emails tagged, logged in a sheet and assigned to staff
Weekly summaries of leads and sales sent to managers

outro.text: Each of these takes minutes to describe but saves hours every month. Our Zapier automation services start with the workflows that remove the most manual work, then add more once your team sees the benefit. We measure time saved before and after, so you know whether each workflow is worth its monthly task cost, and we switch off anything that no longer earns its place.

paragraphs.text: Single workflows are often ready in three to five days. Larger sets of connected workflows take two to four weeks.

Zapier maintenance support covers monitoring, repairs, connection renewals, updates when apps change and small improvements. Plans start from Rs. 3,000 per month, so your automations keep running as your business grows. Each month, you receive a short summary of runs, failures fixed and any changes we recommend to reduce costs or improve overall speed and reliability.

items.q: Can you work inside our existing Zapier account?
items.a: Yes. We usually work directly in your account with team access, so you keep full ownership of every Zap and scenario. If you do not have an account yet, we help you choose the right plan and set it up in your company's name.

items.q: How do you stop workflows from failing silently?
items.a: We add filters, error paths and notification steps that alert a named person by email or Slack when something goes wrong. For important workflows, we also log every run in a sheet, so you can see what was processed and spot gaps quickly.

items.q: Can you move our workflows between platforms?
items.a: Yes. We migrate workflows from Zapier to Make, or from Make to Zapier, when costs or features make a switch worthwhile. We rebuild each workflow, run old and new versions side by side, compare results and switch over only when they match.

items.q: Do we need developers to manage the workflows later?
items.a: Not usually. Zapier and Make are designed for non-technical users, and we document each workflow in plain language. We also offer a short training session, so your team can make simple edits, such as changing an email address or a filter, without help.

items.q: Is our data safe on these platforms?
items.a: Both Zapier and Make use encryption and offer security controls for business accounts. We limit app permissions to what each workflow needs, avoid passing unnecessary personal data and recommend two-factor login for every team member.
